name: The St. Regis Toronto
positioning: Canada's first St. Regis, a downtown Toronto hotel with a 31st-floor restaurant and spa and butler service for every room
best_for: Families wanting spacious rooms, butler service and kids' experiences
Travelers who want a high-floor spa, pool and cocktail bar in the city centre

facts.text: Before becoming a St. Regis, the hotel was a Trump property and then The Adelaide.
LOUIX LOUIS sits 31 floors above the Toronto skyline.
LOUIX LOUIS serves American cuisine with a French twist.
The hotel's take on the Bloody Mary is called the Rouge 140 and is served at LOUIX LOUIS.
Afternoon tea features Midnight Blossom, a bespoke blend made for the hotel by Toronto-based Sloane Fine Tea Merchants.
The 15,000-square-foot spa is on the 31st floor.
Every room and suite has a European-style wet bar and a Nespresso beverage system.
Bathrooms have a rainfall shower, a deep-soaking tub and an in-mirror TV.
The Caroline Astor and John Jacob Astor suites are on the 30th floor, each with a kitchen, living and dining room and two bedrooms.
All rooms come with St. Regis butler service.
Family experiences include a movie and popcorn night, an in-room Wilderness Retreat and Mrs Astor's Little Tea society.

highlights.text: The St. Regis Toronto is Canada's first St. Regis hotel.
LOUIX LOUIS's interior is designed to represent the inside of a crystal whiskey glass, inspired by Toronto's distilling heritage.
At the heart of LOUIX LOUIS is a two-story grand bar showcasing over 500 dark spirits.
The hotel holds a champagne sabering ritual at 6 pm every day in the lobby-level Astor Lounge.
An infinity-edge lap pool and whirlpool are on the 32nd floor, along with a dry sauna and steam room.

considerations.text: Billy Bishop Toronto City Airport is about 3 km away, but the hotel does not provide an airport shuttle.
Self parking and valet parking each cost $70 per day.
WhataHotel notes premium luxury pricing reflecting the high-end positioning.
